title: Choose the world for the Plotted homepage
question: The roll assigned The Evening Round. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Evening Round
options.lineage: the gardener's walk round the garden at the end of the day
options.thesis: The page is one walk down the garden path, and the light changes as you go: high sun, golden hour, rose, dusk.
materials: drenched colour fields that turn with the scroll
engraved single-stroke planting drawn at border scale
your own photographs as windows in the colour
options.viewport: A full-bleed euphorbia-lime field under a pale sky band; the headline set huge in Zodiak italic; a border of engraved plants growing along the bottom edge; Request access on marigold beside it.
options.risk: Four drenched grounds in one page is a lot of colour; if any one band is timid the whole walk reads as a gradient gimmick.

raised.raise: One time-of-day rail runs the whole page; every section registers against it and it doubles as the navigation.
Each stop on the walk owns exactly one truth about the garden: what's in bloom, what the week holds, what to buy, what to plant together, who's visiting.
Colour is flat and total within a band: no tints, no cream fallback anywhere on the page.

options.label: The Seed Rack
options.lineage: lithographed seed packets on a nursery rack
options.thesis: Every feature is a packet on the rack: saturated front, growing instructions on the back.
options.viewport: A wall of packets in full colour, the middle one opened out into the headline and the call to action.
options.risk: Charming and familiar; seed-packet nostalgia is where many garden brands already live.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: theatre lighting on a seamless cyclorama
options.thesis: The garden as a stage lit from night to day: stacked horizon bands, features as lighting cues.
options.viewport: A black field with a cobalt horizon; the headline acquires its shadow as rose light gathers above the band.
options.case: Holds audience identification (gardeners read light) but opens in the dark, which hides the product for a beat too long.
options.risk: Starts black; a gardening product that opens at night can read as a tech demo.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.lineage: glass spectrograms on a viewing box
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one calibrated rail; colour only as hairlines.
options.viewport: A grey band crossed by seven thin bright lines, one per feature.
options.case: Loses both axes: no gardener sees their garden in charcoal.
options.kept: One rail that everything registers against.

options.label: Night Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six gauges, each owning one truth.
options.viewport: Six dials: bloom, weather, frost, birds, jobs, list.
options.case: Loses both axes and breaks a product commitment: no dashboards as scorecards.

options.label: Man-Machine Grid
options.lineage: traffic-signal line diagrams on a strict grid
options.thesis: Features wired together as a neon schematic.
options.viewport: A wiring diagram joining catalogue, schemes and list.
options.case: Clear about how the parts connect, but cold; gardeners would not recognise themselves.
options.kept: Total commitment to flat, untinted colour.

options.label: Sixteen-Colour Field
options.thesis: A garden sunset built from dithered pixel pairs.
options.viewport: A dithered dusk with a text window docked low.
options.case: Loses both axes: retro-computing is not this audience's world.
options.kept: Regions that hold their place while their contents change.

options.label: Raku Smoke
options.thesis: Soot black and crackled white with one ember.
options.viewport: A black ground with one ember-orange vessel.
options.case: Loses both axes: monochrome against a brief that asks for full bloom.
options.kept: Asymmetry accepted as a rule of composition.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Cream paper, serif headline, a phone mockup and three feature cards.
canonCard.viewport: Headline left, garden photograph right, Request access below.
canonCard.risk: It is the page you have now.
